### CVE-2016-1646
- Assigner: Chrome | Published: 2016-03-29 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-06-08, ransomware=Unknown — Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Read Vulnerability

The Array.prototype.concat implementation in builtins.cc in Google V8, as used in Google Chrome before 49.0.2623.108, does not properly consider element data types, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted JavaScript code.

- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2016-5131
- Assigner: Chrome | Published: 2016-07-23 | Updated: 2026-10-14 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Use-after-free vulnerability in libxml2 through 2.9.4, as used in Google Chrome before 52.0.2743.82, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via vectors related to the XPointer range-to function.

### CVE-2016-5195
- Assigner: Chrome | Published: 2016-11-10 | Updated: 2025-11-04 | Max CVSS: 7
- CWE: n/a; CWE-362 CWE-362 Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-03-03, ransomware=Unknown — Linux Kernel Race Condition Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 40616: Linux Kernel 2.6.22 < 3.9 (x86/x64) - 'Dirty COW /proc/self/mem' Race Condition Privilege Escalation (SUID Method) (local/linux, 2016-10-21, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 40847: Linux Kernel 2.6.22 < 3.9 - 'Dirty COW /proc/self/mem' Race Condition Privilege Escalation (/etc/passwd Method) (local/linux, 2016-11-27, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 40838: Linux Kernel 2.6.22 < 3.9 - 'Dirty COW PTRACE_POKEDATA' Race Condition (Write Access Method) (local/linux, 2016-10-26, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 40839: Linux Kernel 2.6.22 < 3.9 - 'Dirty COW' 'PTRACE_POKEDATA' Race Condition Privilege Escalation (/etc/passwd Method) (local/linux, 2016-11-28, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 40611: Linux Kernel 2.6.22 < 3.9 - 'Dirty COW' /proc/self/mem Race Condition (Write Access Method) (local/linux, 2016-10-19, verified=1)

Race condition in mm/gup.c in the Linux kernel 2.x through 4.x before 4.8.3 allows local users to gain privileges by leveraging incorrect handling of a copy-on-write (COW) feature to write to a read-only memory mapping, as exploited in the wild in October 2016, aka "Dirty COW."

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2016-5198
- Assigner: Chrome | Published: 2017-01-19 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: incorrect compiler optimisations; CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-06-08, ransomware=Unknown — Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Memory Vulnerability

V8 in Google Chrome prior to 54.0.2840.90 for Linux, and 54.0.2840.85 for Android, and 54.0.2840.87 for Windows and Mac included incorrect optimisation assumptions, which allowed a remote attacker to perform arbitrary read/write operations, leading to code execution, via a crafted HTML page.

Affected:
- n/a / Google Chrome prior to 54.0.2840.90 for Linux, and 54.0.2840.85 for Android, and 54.0.2840.87 for Windows and Mac: affected Google Chrome prior to 54.0.2840.90 for Linux, and 54.0.2840.85 for Android, and 54.0.2840.87 for Windows and Mac
